Introduced this function at clippy's request (cyclomatic complexity of main function). 

An alternative refactor would be to extract larger functions (e.g. `add_ahead_behind_segments`, `add_stashed_segment`, `add_other_segments`). 

Suggestions welcome

What about nesting the symbol? e.g. `deleted = { symbol="x", count=true }`
Can you just pass a mutable reference of repo_status instead of giving the whole ownership to the function and returning it?

What do you think about
```toml
[git_status]
staged_count = true
deleted_count = true
untracked_count = false
```

and then we would get segment-specific styling for free with #378:
```toml
[git_status]
staged_count = true
staged_count.style = "green"
```

Note that this is invalid in `toml`. You cannot give both a `boolean` and a `table` value to the same key.

Either use this:

```toml
[git_status]
staged_count_enabled = true
staged_count.style = "green"
```

or this:

```toml
[git_status]
staged_count = { enabled = true, style = "green" }
# also: staged = { style = "red", symbol = "=", count = { enabled = true, style = "green" }}
```

or you can display the count only when style exists using `fn new_segment_if_config_exists`

```toml
staged_count_style = "green" # will display staged_count
# will not display untracked count
```

IDK. Personally, I think one should always benchmark and consider multi-threading / async when one uses speed as an argument but I'm also fine with leaving it as it is.
#383 is merged now! May be the refactored configs [here](https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/master/starship/src/configs/rust.rs) can give you some inspirations :)

I'd prefer we didn't. Anything that touches the filesystem should be ignored in the tests (in practice, we use `#[ignore]` as a proxy for 'don't run on user machines'), because any user looking to do a regular install may run them.

We've already had one bug where (improperly) non-ignored git tests overwrote a bunch of people's git configs with nonsense data.

Merged master and started using the new configs (work in progress).

Decided to go with 
```toml
[git_status]
staged_count_disabled = false
```
I've left "per-segment" styling out of this PR to keep simple. I can see wanting to style both the symbol and count and not obvious to me what the config should look like. So I've chosen simple for now. Also chose `disabled` since it is used elsewhere.
@bijancn Made immutable. Some informal testing with 50,000 untracked files showed no measurable difference vs mutable.
@chipbuster Added back the `#[ignore]`'s
